ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, it is given that $AB=8$, $BC=12$. Points $O$ and $P$ are the midpoints of sides $AB$ and $AD$, respectively. Point $H$ is a moving point on side $CD$. Connect $OH$. Quadrilateral $OBCH$ is folded along $OH$ to obtain quadrilateral $OFEH$. Connect $PE$. What is the minimum value of the length of $PE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect EO, PO, OC, \\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore \angle B=\angle OAP=90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ Points O, P are the midpoints of sides AB, AD respectively, \\
$\therefore$ OB=AO=4, AP=DP=6, \\
In $\triangle OBC$, BC=12, OB=4, \\
$\therefore$ OC=$\sqrt{OB^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{4^2+12^2}=4\sqrt{10}$, \\
In $\triangle AOP$, OA=4, PA=6, \\
$\therefore$ OP=$\sqrt{OA^2+PA^2}=\sqrt{4^2+6^2}=2\sqrt{13}$, \\
Due to folding, OE=OC=$4\sqrt{10}$, \\
$\because$ PE$\geq$ OE−OP, \\
$\therefore$ The minimum value of PE=OE−OP=$4\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt{13}$, \\
Thus, the answer is: $PE_{\min} = \boxed{4\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt{13}}$.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate-angle sweep of the fold. Read from the diagram that AB is vertical, BC is horizontal, H slides on the right side CD, and C reflects to E across line OH. Set coordinates B=(0,0), A=(0,8), C=(12,0), D=(12,8). Then O=(0,4) and P=(6,8). Let the crease OH have angle phi with the positive x-axis. Since H=(12,t) with 0<=t<=8, tan phi=(t-4)/12, so phi ranges from -alpha to alpha, where alpha=arctan(1/3). The ray OC has direction angle -alpha. Reflecting C across a line of angle phi sends the direction of OE to theta=2phi-(-alpha)=2phi+alpha, so theta ranges from -alpha to 3alpha. The direction of OP is beta=arctan(4/6)=arctan(2/3), and beta lies in this interval because 0<beta<3alpha, e.g. tan(3alpha)=13/9>2/3. Thus some allowed H makes E lie exactly on the ray OP. Also OE=OC=sqrt(12^2+4^2)=4sqrt(10), while OP=sqrt(6^2+4^2)=2sqrt(13). Among points E on the fixed circle centered at O with radius OE, the closest point to P occurs when E is on the ray OP beyond P, giving PE=OE-OP=4sqrt(10)-2sqrt(13).
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：附图中，ABCD 是一个竖直放置的矩形，AB 在左侧、CD 在右侧、BC 在下方，A、D 在上方。O 位于 AB 的中点附近，P 位于 AD 的中点附近，H 位于右侧 CD 上。折叠后，折痕是 OH，点 C 被折到上方的点 E，点 B 被折到左上方的点 F，并且图中连接了 PE。推理：按图示取坐标 B=(0,0), A=(0,8), C=(12,0), D=(12,8)，则 O=(0,4)，P=(6,8)。设折痕 OH 与 x 轴正方向的夹角为 phi。因为 H=(12,t), 0<=t<=8，所以 tan phi=(t-4)/12，故 phi 从 -alpha 到 alpha 变化，其中 alpha=arctan(1/3)。向量 OC=(12,-4)，其方向角为 -alpha。折叠即点 C 关于直线 OH 反射到 E，因此 OE 的方向角 theta=2phi-(-alpha)=2phi+alpha，所以 theta 的范围是 [-alpha,3alpha]。向量 OP=(6,4)，其方向角 beta=arctan(4/6)=arctan(2/3)。由于 0<beta，且 tan(3alpha)=13/9>2/3，所以 beta<3alpha，因此 beta 落在允许的 theta 范围内；也就是说，可以取某个 H，使得 E 正好位于射线 OP 上。折叠保持距离，OE=OC=sqrt(12^2+4^2)=4sqrt(10)，而 OP=sqrt(6^2+4^2)=2sqrt(13)。所有可能的 E 都在以 O 为圆心、半径 OE 的圆上；当 E 的方向与 OP 同向时，PE 最小，此时 E 在射线 OP 上且在 P 的外侧，所以 PE_min=OE-OP=4sqrt(10)-2sqrt(13)。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, it is given that $AB=8$ and $BC=12$. Points $O$ and $P$ are the midpoints of sides $AB$ and $AD$, respectively. Point $H$ is a moving point on side $CD$. Connect $OH$. Quadrilateral $OBCH$ is folded along $OH$ to obtain quadrilateral $OFEH$. Connect $PE$. What is the minimum value of the length of $PE$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect $EO$, $PO$, $OC$. \\
$\because$ $ABCD$ is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore \angle B=\angle OAP=90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ points $O$ and $P$ are the midpoints of sides $AB$ and $AD$ respectively, \\
$\therefore$ $OB=AO=4$, $AP=DP=6$, \\
In $\triangle OBC$, $BC=12$, $OB=4$, \\
$\therefore$ $OC=\sqrt{OB^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{4^2+12^2}=4\sqrt{10}$, \\
In $\triangle AOP$, $OA=4$, $PA=6$, \\
$\therefore$ $OP=\sqrt{OA^2+PA^2}=\sqrt{4^2+6^2}=2\sqrt{13}$, \\
Due to folding, $OE=OC=4\sqrt{10}$, \\
$\because$ $PE\geq OE-OP$, \\
$\therefore$ the minimum value of $PE=OE-OP=4\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt{13}$, \\
Thus, $PE_{\min}=\boxed{4\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt{13}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, a dashed rectangle ABCD can be seen, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right; O is on the left side AB, P is on the upper side AD, and H is on the right side CD. In the folded figure, the crease is OH, the original C is folded to E, the original B is folded to F, and PE is connected. Reasoning: In rectangle ABCD, AB=8 and BC=12. O is the midpoint of AB, so OA=OB=4; P is the midpoint of AD, and AD=BC=12, so AP=PD=6. Connect OC, OP, OE. Because ∠OBC=90°, OC=√(OB^2+BC^2)=√(4^2+12^2)=4√10. Because ∠OAP=90°, OP=√(OA^2+AP^2)=√(4^2+6^2)=2√13. The folding is carried out along OH, O is on the crease and does not move, and C is folded to E, therefore the folding preserves distance OE=OC=4√10. In triangle OPE, by the triangle inequality PE ≥ OE−OP, so PE ≥ 4√10−2√13. When E is located on ray OP and outside P, equality can be taken; at this time the crease OH is the angle bisector of ∠COE, and this angle bisector starting from O can intersect side CD at an allowed point H, so equality can be reached. Therefore the minimum value of PE is 4√10−2√13.
